question: Deep-verifying the external deterministic-compilation and witnessed-determinism literature and artifacts that SPIDER is about to treat as its decisive economic baseline: for Agentic Compilation, TraceCompiler, Auto/AGI Compiler, and tool-schema compression work, what are the exact reported determinism or witnessed-fraction, precision/recall, per-workflow and per-compilation cost, abstention and refusal numbers; are those numbers reported on a task distribution comparable to SPIDER's; which artifacts are actually obtainable and runnable with no LLM API key, no browser and no docker, and which require external model access; and -- the decision-relevant verdict -- does the external convergence constitute a FALSIFICATION of SPIDER's compilation-bypass and inheritance direction (i.e. an external system already achieves, or provably can achieve, the cost profile SPIDER is chasing without accumulating inherited mechanisms), or merely a sign that SPIDER's own measurements have been invalid and uninformative? Additionally, a bounded check of the published cross-site and hierarchical-transfer evidence sufficient to tell SPIDER whether flat fragment reuse is a defensible level of description for cross-site transfer or a known failure mode, so that the Graph and Frontier budgets are not spent rediscovering a published bound.
hypothesis: H_EXTERNAL_COMPILATION_VERIFICATION (C-PRODUCT-ECON, PIVOT, cognitive_reset true, SUPERSEDE): The external deterministic-compilation literature (Agentic Compilation, TraceCompiler, Auto/AGI Compiler, tool-schema compression) reports specific quantitative claims about witnessed-determinism fractions, precision/recall, compilation costs, and abstention rates. These claims can be verified against primary sources (papers, repos, artifacts) without requiring LLM API keys, browser automation, or Docker. The verification will produce: (1) a pinned, source-verified baseline specification with exact numbers for each system; (2) an explicit partition of which artifacts are runnable locally (stdlib-only, no external dependencies) versus which require external model access; (3) the smallest next action for any unobtainable artifact; (4) a stated recommended strong baseline for the no-memory deterministic executor arm that Frontier and Product will use; (5) a bounded assessment of published cross-site and hierarchical-transfer evidence to determine whether flat fragment reuse is a defensible level of description for cross-site transfer or a known failure mode. If the external convergence constitutes a falsification of SPIDER's compilation-bypass direction, this experiment will establish that with primary-source evidence; if it merely indicates SPIDER's measurements have been invalid, this experiment will establish that instead.
falsifier: H falsified if: (a) primary sources for any of the four target systems (Agentic Compilation, TraceCompiler, Auto/AGI Compiler, tool-schema compression) cannot be located or accessed after exhaustive search of published papers, GitHub repos, and supplementary materials; (b) reported quantitative claims (witnessed-determinism fraction, precision/recall, per-workflow cost, per-compilation cost, abstention rate, refusal rate) cannot be extracted with source citations (paper section, table, figure, repo commit, artifact hash); (c) the runnable-locally versus requires-model-access partition cannot be determined for each system's artifacts; (d) the bounded cross-site/hierarchical-transfer evidence check fails to produce a clear determination (with citations) on whether flat fragment reuse is defensible or a known failure mode; (e) the recommended strong baseline for the no-memory deterministic executor cannot be specified with concrete parameters and expected performance bounds. Measurement invalidity triggers if any mandatory verification step (source location, claim extraction, runnability assessment, cross-site evidence assessment) cannot be completed due to infrastructure failure rather than absence of evidence.

baselines.description: SPIDER's current compilation-bypass and inheritance direction as reflected in frozen experiment history: 17-deep alias-catalog/routing/WebMCP tunnel at pooled 21/40=0.525 Wilson [0.352,0.648] with 0/10 mixed routing gain 0.0; valid non-Pareto falsification of residual-novelty economics under honest counters (EXP-FRONTIER-36042599040 PASS, rho 0.4837 ECE 0.216); Intel 29-streak C-CROSSSITE without WebGym diverse; Physics 77+ attempts 0 real-Web hits. This is the internal baseline the external literature must be compared against.

The no-memory deterministic executor that will serve as the mandatory strong baseline arm for Frontier and Product experiments: a compile-once deterministic workflow IR with O(1) amortized execution cost, invariant-enforcing protocol (pre/post-condition guards, ordering validation), and cost-optimal planner. This baseline must be specified with concrete parameters (expected compilation cost, hot-path latency, token cost, compilation success rate) derived from the verified external literature.

The flat fragment reuse level of description for cross-site transfer: reusable mechanisms as flat action sequences or parameterized templates without hierarchical Intent/Stage/Action decomposition. This is the level of description SPIDER's Graph and Frontier lanes have been implicitly testing. The bounded cross-site evidence check will determine if this is defensible or a known failure mode in the external literature.

The hierarchical Intent/Stage/Action with pre/post-condition validation level of description for cross-site transfer (as reported in Agentic Compilation and related work). This is the alternative level of description that external convergence suggests may be necessary. The bounded evidence check will assess whether published evidence favors this over flat fragment reuse.

positive_control: PC-SOURCE-VERIFICATION: For each of the four target systems (Agentic Compilation, TraceCompiler, Auto/AGI Compiler, tool-schema compression), at least one primary source (peer-reviewed paper, preprint with DOI/arXiv ID, or GitHub repo with verifiable commit) must be located and the key quantitative claims extracted with exact citations. The positive control passes if all four systems have at least one verifiable primary source with extractable quantitative claims.
null_control: NC-NO-EXTERNAL-CONVERGENCE: The null hypothesis that there is no convergent external evidence for deterministic compilation bypass achieving the cost profile SPIDER is chasing. This null is rejected if the verification finds convergent quantitative claims across multiple independent groups (Agentic Compilation, TraceCompiler, Auto/AGI Compiler, tool-schema compression) that collectively specify a cost profile (compilation cost, execution cost, success rate, abstention rate) that dominates SPIDER's current internal baseline. The null control passes (i.e., no falsification of SPIDER's direction) if the external claims are either unverifiable, not convergent, or do not dominate the internal baseline when adjusted for task distribution differences.
measurement_validity: MV1_SOURCE_LOCATION: Each target system must have at least one primary source located with permanent identifier (DOI, arXiv ID, GitHub commit hash, Zenodo record). Search documented with query, date, and result.

MV2_CLAIM_EXTRACTION: For each located source, the following quantitative claims must be extracted with exact citation (section/table/figure/commit): witnessed-determinism fraction or equivalent, precision/recall on stated benchmarks, per-workflow compilation cost (time, tokens, compute), per-compilation cost (amortized), abstention rate, refusal rate. Claims not found are explicitly recorded as 'not reported' with source location searched.

MV3_TASK_DISTRIBUTION_COMPARABILITY: For each extracted claim, the task distribution (benchmark, number of tasks, sites, complexity metrics) must be documented and compared to SPIDER's synthetic 40-task alias-OOD (30 orthogonal header/body/auth + 10 mixed) and WebArena-Verified/WebGym distributions. Comparability assessment recorded as: comparable / partially comparable / not comparable / unknown with justification.

MV4_RUNNABILITY_ASSESSMENT: For each system's artifacts (released code, models, datasets, IR specifications), determine: runnable locally with stdlib only (no LLM API key, no browser, no docker) / runnable with local model weights only / requires external LLM API / requires browser automation / requires Docker/container / not released / unknown. Assessment based on repo README, release artifacts, paper supplementary, direct inspection.

MV5_CROSS_SITE_EVIDENCE_CHECK: Bounded search of published literature (papers, surveys, benchmarks) for evidence on cross-site transfer and hierarchical vs flat fragment reuse. Search terms: cross-site transfer web agents, hierarchical decomposition web navigation, intent-stage-action web, fragment reuse across websites, website holdout generalization. At least 10 relevant papers/surveys screened. Determination: flat fragment reuse defensible / flat fragment reuse known failure mode / hierarchical necessary / evidence insufficient / mixed. Each determination backed by specific citations.

MV6_BASELINE_SPECIFICATION: A complete recommended strong baseline specification for the no-memory deterministic executor arm must be produced with: expected compilation cost (ms, tokens), hot-path execution latency (ms), token cost per repeat invocation, compilation success rate, abstention/refusal behavior, invariant protocol parameters (pre/post-condition check types, ordering validation), cost-optimal planner parameters. All parameters traced to verified external sources or explicitly marked as SPIDER-inferred with justification.
decision_rule: Frozen three-way decision after measurement validity check: (A) MEASUREMENT_INVALID if any mandatory MV1-MV6 step fails due to infrastructure failure (network, disk, compute) rather than absence of evidence. Absence of evidence is a valid scientific outcome recorded in results. (B) SUPPORTS_FALSIFICATION if: all four target systems have verifiable primary sources (MV1 PASS), quantitative claims extracted (MV2 PASS), runnability assessed (MV4 PASS), cross-site evidence check yields determination (MV5 PASS), baseline specified (MV6 PASS), AND the verified external convergence constitutes a falsification of SPIDER's compilation-bypass direction (i.e., external systems demonstrably achieve or provably can achieve the target cost profile without inherited mechanisms, on comparable or harder task distributions). (C) SUPPORTS_INVALID_MEASUREMENTS if: verification completes (MV1-MV6 PASS) but external convergence does NOT falsify SPIDER's direction (claims unverifiable, not convergent, not dominating, or task distribution incomparable), indicating SPIDER's measurements have been invalid/uninformative. (D) MIXED if verification partially completes (some systems verified, others not) or cross-site evidence is mixed/insufficient. (E) INCONCLUSIVE if verification cannot reach a determination due to fundamental ambiguity in external claims.
product_consequence_positive: If SUPPORTS_FALSIFICATION: SPIDER's compilation-bypass and inheritance direction is falsified by external convergence. The no-memory deterministic executor (as specified in MV6) becomes the authorized strong baseline for all lanes. Graph and Frontier budgets must pivot away from flat fragment reuse (if MV5 determines it is a known failure mode) toward hierarchical Intent/Stage/Action with pre/post-condition validation. Product economics gate (C-PRODUCT-ECON) must be re-evaluated against the verified external cost profile. C-PRODUCT-ECON status updated based on whether SPIDER can still claim residual-novelty economics against a verified stronger baseline. Intel delivers the pinned baseline specification as a Codex-accepted artifact for all lanes.
product_consequence_negative: If SUPPORTS_INVALID_MEASUREMENTS: SPIDER's compilation-bypass direction is NOT falsified by external literature; the external convergence is either weak, incomparable, or unverifiable. The no-memory deterministic executor baseline (MV6) is still specified but calibrated to SPIDER's task distribution. Graph and Frontier may continue flat fragment reuse if MV5 finds it defensible, or must pivot if MV5 finds it a known failure mode. The 15-experiment C-CROSSSITE census hunt is explicitly ended (parked per Director mandate) with the design-level question answered: flat vs hierarchical transfer level of description is determined by published evidence, not by another acquisition attempt. Intel delivers the verified baseline specification and cross-site evidence assessment as Codex-accepted artifacts.
estimated_cost: Compute: 2-4 hours wall time for literature search, source verification, claim extraction, runnability testing (stdlib-only), cross-site evidence screening, and baseline specification writing. No LLM API calls, no browser automation, no Docker, no GPU. Network: HTTP requests to arXiv, GitHub, DOI resolvers, publisher APIs (public endpoints only). Artifact storage: <50 MB for PDFs, repo metadata, extracted claims JSON. USD: ~$1-2 GitHub runner.
expected_information_gain: Very high per cost. This is the single highest-leverage Intel work per Director mandate: two active scientific lanes (Frontier's span-level economics, Product's A->B transfer) will spend their entire budget against a no-memory compiled executor that is currently an SPIDER-authored strawman. If that baseline is weak/misreported/dominates inheritance, both lanes are wasted; if correctly specified, both lanes become decisive. This experiment also ends Intel's 15-experiment C-CROSSSITE census hunt by answering the design-level question (flat vs hierarchical transfer) that was blocking progress. The verification is runnable in this environment with no unavailable assets.
